# Disagreement Log — 1 Kings Chapter 13
**Reviewed by:** SOPHIA | **Date:** 2026-03-11

---

## Summary
26 verse(s) flagged for significant translation divergence.

### Verse 1
**EMET (literal):** And-behold, a-man-of God came from-Judah by-the-word-of YHWH to Bethel, and-Jeroboam was-standing by the-altar to-burn-incense.

**LOGOS (formal):** And behold, a man of God came out of Judah by the word of the LORD to Bethel. Jeroboam was standing by the altar to make offerings.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Just then, a man of God arrived from Judah at Bethel, sent by the word of the LORD. Jeroboam was standing at the altar, about to make an offering.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 3
**EMET (literal):** And-he-gave on-that day a-sign, saying, "This is the-sign that YHWH has-spoken: Behold, the-altar will-be-torn, and-the-ashes that are upon-it will-be-poured-out."

**LOGOS (formal):** And he gave a sign the same day, saying, "This is the sign that the LORD has spoken: 'Behold, the altar shall be torn down, and the ashes that are on it shall be poured out.'"

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** That same day the man gave a confirming sign: "This is the proof that the LORD has spoken: this altar will split apart, and the ashes on it will spill out."

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 4
**EMET (literal):** And-it-was when-the-king heard ʾet-the-word-of the-man-of God that he-called against the-altar in-Bethel, and-Jeroboam stretched-out ʾet-his-hand from-upon the-altar, saying, "Seize-him!" And-his-hand that he-stretched-out against-him dried-up, and-he-was-not able to-return-it to-himself.

**LOGOS (formal):** And when the king heard the saying of the man of God, which he cried against the altar at Bethel, Jeroboam stretched out his hand from the altar, saying, "Seize him." And his hand, which he stretched out against him, dried up, so that he could not draw it back to himself.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** When King Jeroboam heard the man of God's words against the altar at Bethel, he pointed at him from the altar and ordered, "Arrest him!" But the hand he stretched out shriveled up, and he couldn't pull it back.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 5
**EMET (literal):** And-the-altar was-torn, and-the-ashes poured-out from the-altar, according-to-the-sign that the-man-of God gave by-the-word-of YHWH.

**LOGOS (formal):** The altar also was torn down, and the ashes poured out from the altar, according to the sign that the man of God had given by the word of the LORD.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** The altar split apart and the ashes spilled out, exactly as the sign the man of God had announced by the LORD's word.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 6
**EMET (literal):** And-the-king answered and-said to the-man-of God, "Plead, please, the-face-of YHWH your-God, and-pray for-me, and-let-my-hand return to-me." And-the-man-of God pleaded ʾet-the-face-of YHWH, and-the-hand-of the-king returned to-him and-was as-before.

**LOGOS (formal):** And the king said to the man of God, "Entreat now the favor of the LORD your God, and pray for me, that my hand may be restored to me." And the man of God entreated the LORD, and the king's hand was restored to him and became as it was before.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** The king pleaded with the man of God, "Please pray to the LORD your God for me — ask him to restore my hand." The man of God prayed, and the king's hand was restored to normal.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 8
**EMET (literal):** And-the-man-of God said to the-king, "If you-give to-me ʾet-half your-house, I-will-not come with-you, and-I-will-not eat bread and-I-will-not drink water in-this place.

**LOGOS (formal):** And the man of God said to the king, "If you give me half your house, I will not go in with you. And I will not eat bread or drink water in this place,

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** But the man of God told the king, "Even if you gave me half of everything you own, I would not go with you, and I would not eat or drink anything here.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 9
**EMET (literal):** For so he-commanded-me by-the-word-of YHWH, saying, 'You-shall-not eat bread and-you-shall-not drink water, and-you-shall-not return by-the-way that you-came.'"

**LOGOS (formal):** for so was it commanded me by the word of the LORD, saying, 'You shall neither eat bread nor drink water nor return by the way that you came.'"

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** The LORD gave me strict orders: 'Do not eat bread, do not drink water, and do not return by the same route you came.'"

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 10
**EMET (literal):** And-he-went by-another way, and-did-not return by-the-way that he-came to-Bethel.

**LOGOS (formal):** So he went another way and did not return by the way that he came to Bethel.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** So he took a different road and did not go back the way he had come to Bethel.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 12
**EMET (literal):** And-their-father spoke to-them, "Which way did-he-go?" And-his-sons had-seen ʾet-the-way that the-man-of God who-came from-Judah went.

**LOGOS (formal):** And their father said to them, "Which way did he go?" And his sons showed him the way that the man of God who came from Judah had gone.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Their father asked, "Which road did he take?" His sons had watched which direction the man of God from Judah had gone.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 14
**EMET (literal):** And-he-went after the-man-of God and-found-him sitting under a-terebinth. And-he-said to-him, "Are-you the-man-of God who-came from-Judah?" And-he-said, "I am."

**LOGOS (formal):** And he went after the man of God and found him sitting under an oak. And he said to him, "Are you the man of God who came from Judah?" And he said, "I am."

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** He caught up with the man of God, who was sitting under an oak tree. "Are you the man of God from Judah?" he asked. "I am," the man replied.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

— SOPHIA
